# The Classics Never Go Out of Style: An Empirical Study of Downgrades from the Bazel Build Technology


# Purpose
This replication package enables the replication of the study "The Classics Never Go Out of Style: An Empirical Study of Downgrades from the Bazel Build Technology", accepted to ICSE2024. The study explores the phenomenon of build system downgrades, i.e., projects that move from a feature-rich modern build tool to a more traditional one (e.g., Bazel to Make). Surprisingly, the paper shows that, in the context of Bazel, downgrades happen regularly—roughly 11.2% of the studied projects that adopted Bazel downgraded to a less feature-rich alternative. The study also characterizes downgrades according to seven emergent themes, analyzed what tools replaced Bazel in the downgrading projects, and studied the generalizability of the themes using a confirmatory context (downgrades from Gradle) and a contradictory context (upgrades to Bazel).

## Artifact Available

We have made our replication package publicly available on zenodo.org.

## Artifact Reusable
We have provided detailed documentation on the step-by-step execution of the study. All outputs from which the results in the paper have been compiled are also included and documented.
The replication package supports easy execution of the analyses for verification of the artifact, as well as a replicable process from scratch.


# Provenance
The package includes the code for the artifact and the dataset used in the study. We have provided docker images which will automatically setup various modules of our package (therefore docker is the only dependency). The docker can be easily setup on a Mac or Linux machine by directly applying the commands in the README of the replication package in order. Therefore, there are no particular technology skills assumed by the reviewer. The expected setup time for the docker is a few minutes. Below, we provide more details on the package structure.

## Package Structure
This package contains three main folders under the main folder (`build-downgrade`):

- *study-input*: holds data files required to run the artifact. These files contain the list of analyzed repositories in the study.  There are two files:
   - `project-dataset.csv`: contains a subset of the dataset for the purpose of artifact evaluation. We rely on this file to run the analysis.
   - `project-dataset-full.csv`: contains the full dataset. Note that both datasets are obtained directly from a prior work [1].

- *study-output*: holds results that will be produced after running the package. The folder will produce the following outputs:
   - `clonned_repos`: holds folders of clonned repositories to be analyzed.
   - `current.csv`: holds data related to projects that adopt the Bazel build system. This file can be seen under the `results` folder after running the docker images.
   - `abandoned.csv`: holds data related to projects that abandoned the Bazel build system. This file can be seen under the `results` folder after running the docker images.
   - `number-aband-projects.pdf`: Barplot showing the distribution of projects abandoning Bazel. 
   - `duration-aband-projects.pdf`: Boxplot showing the distribution of the duration of Bazel adoption.

- *study*: holds four folders that contain scripts and files relevant to the analysis of the study.
   - [1.quantitative-analysis] contains scripts to clone project repositories and analyze projects that adopt/abandon Bazel.
   - [2.ploting] contains an R script that produces two plots mentioned above in the *study-output* section.
   - [3.thematic-analysis] contains a data file (excel file) related to the thematic analysis in the study.
   - [4.analytic-generalizability-analysis] contains a data file (excel file) related to the analytic generalizability analysis in the study.

References:

[1] Ma Yuxing, Tapajit Dey, Chris Bogart, Sadika Amreen, Marat Valiev, Adam Tutko, David Kennard, Russell Zaretzki, and Audris Mockus. "World of code: enabling a research workflow for mining and analyzing the universe of open source VCS data." Empirical Software Engineering 26 (2021): 1-42.


# Setup

## Software requirements

The following software is required to run this replication package:

## For evaluation of the artifacts

- Docker version 24.0.6, build ed223bc820
- Tested on *macOS* and *Ubuntu* only. Use on Windows machines may require conversion of some commands to make them compatible. Please see more details on this in the *Machines Spec.* section at the end of this file.

## For replication of the study in subsequent research

> **_NOTE:_** This is not required for artifact evaluation. It is provided to facilitate future reuse and repurposing of the replication package and is equivalent to running the same analysis in the evaluation of the artifacts in users' customized environments.

- Python version 3.10.2
- R version 4.2.1

All the other requirements have been satisfied via in-script installations.

## Hardware requirement

- Architecture arm64 or amd64 (We tested the artifact on machines with the specifications mentioned below in the Machines Specs section.)
- Preferably RAM > 16GB
- Free Hard Disk Space > 20GB
- Preferably CPU Cores > 8

## Installation
0. Make sure you have [Bash](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bash_(Unix_shell)>) installed on your system.

1. Extract the files in the compressed file "build-downgrade.zip" and put them inside a folder on your machine.

2. Install [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/). Note that we are using version 24.0.6, build ed223bc820.

3. In your Bash command line when connected to the internet, run the following commands to pull the [Docker images](https://hub.docker.com/repositories/malfadel)

   ```
   > docker pull malfadel/python-pandas
   > docker pull malfadel/rstudio-ggplot

   ```
4. In your Bash command line, run the following command to verify that you have successfully loaded the images.
   The docker image names must be listed in the output.

   ```
   > docker images
   ```

5. Your environment is ready to run the analyses. Please make sure that you clear your docker caches 

> > **_NOTE:_** Although it is not recommended, please note that you can build your own docker images by referring to the `commands.sh` and running the docker buildx commands. However, we recommend only pulling the images that we already built and running the commands.


# Usage
We have four main commands needed to run for this replication package:

1. Open the BASH terminal and ensure that you navigate to the directory where the extracted folder is located. This ensures that you execute commands from within the directory, specifically by changing the current directory to be inside the **build-downgrade** folder.

2. In your Bash command line and under the same directory, run the following commands to clone the studied repositories:
    
    ```
       > docker run -it --rm -w /study/1.quantitative-analysis/ -v ${PWD}/study:/study/:ro -v ${PWD}/study-input:/study-input/:ro -v ${PWD}/study-output:/study-output/:rw malfadel/python-pandas python3 1.clone_repo.py
    ```
   The output is the list of cloned repositories in the **clonned_repos** file.

3. In your Bash command line and under the same directory, run the following commands to generate the list of repositories adopting Bazel
    
    ```
       > docker run -it --rm -w /study/1.quantitative-analysis/ -v ${PWD}/study:/study/:ro -v ${PWD}/study-input:/study-input/:ro -v ${PWD}/study-output:/study-output/:rw malfadel/python-pandas python3 2.find_current.py
    ```
